title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (this page and the previous and next pages): Ĝ is the profinite completion of SL(2,Z), presented by torsion generators ρ and σ. σ has order 4 with σ² = -1, and -1 is central. Products such as ε0 = σρ and ε1 are the parabolic ('lacet') elements, with l1 = ε1².

B_{ρ,σ} is the set of pairs (u, μ) where:
- u is an automorphism of Ĝ and μ ∈ Ẑ*, with μ odd;
- u(ρ) = int(α)(ρ) is conjugate to a power of ρ;
- u(σ) = ε2(μ)·int(β)(σ) is conjugate to σ^μ;
- the 'loop relation' (11) holds: u(ε0) = ε0^μ.

So B_{ρ,σ} is a Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group of automorphisms of the profinite modular group. Each such u acts on the cusp, or equivalently on the inertia at infinity, by the cyclotomic-type exponent μ.

The previous page shows that (u, μ) is determined by (α, β, μ). It is even determined by u alone when n ↦ ε0^n is injective, because μ can then be read off from the action on the image of Ẑ. This page opens by noting that μ determines ε = ε2(μ), so the element of B_{ρ,σ} is fixed by α and β alone.

Grothendieck then asks which triples (α, β, μ), or equivalently (ξ, η, μ) with ξ = [α, ρ] and η = ε2(μ)·[β, σ], actually come from an element of B_{ρ,σ}. There are two conditions:
1. There must exist a (unique) automorphism u with u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ησ. This is a condition on ξ and η only.
2. Relation (11) must be expressed in terms of ξ and η.

The boxed computation tries to do the second step. It writes u(ε0) = -u(σ^{-1})u(ρ) as an expression in y, ξ and ρ, then derives ξσ(y) = ε0^{μ-1} and then yσ(y) = 1. It is struck through with diagonal lines and marked 'Faux' (or similar), so it is abandoned.

Grothendieck restarts with ε0' = σ^{-1}ρ = -ε0:
- Since μ is odd, ε0'^μ = (-1)^μ ε0^μ = -ε0^μ.
- Since u(-1) = -1 (lemma (17) on the next page: u(σ²) = int(α)(σ'²) = -1), we get u(ε0') = -u(ε0).
- Hence (11) is equivalent to (16): u(ε0') = ε0'^μ.

Rewriting (16) with the same computation leads, on the next page, to the boxed loop relation ξ = η·l1^ν with ν = (μ-1)/2. It also leads to a corollary: the map (u, μ) ↦ (ξ, η, μ) is injective from B_{ρ,σ} into Ĝ × Ĝ × Ẑ*. Its image is the set Σ^eff of triples satisfying the conjugacy conditions and the loop relation.

The overall purpose is a Drinfeld-style parametrisation, (λ, f) ↔ (μ, ξ, η), of the 'Teichmüller group in genus 1, one point' acting on profinite SL2(Z).
errors: The boxed computation, ending in the conclusion yσ(y) = 1 labelled (15), is struck through and marked as false by Grothendieck. It mixes the use of σ(·) as inner conjugation with the identity σ^{-1} = -σ. It is superseded by the cleaner reduction through ε0' = σ^{-1}ρ.
The equation number (15) is reused: it already labels the map Ẑ → Ĝ on the previous page. Likewise (16) and (17) are reused on the next page. These are notational slips only.
The argument relies on u(-1) = -1, which is proved only afterwards (next page, lemma (17)). The reasoning is not circular, since the lemma uses only that u(σ) is conjugate to an odd power of σ.

ideas.what: Parametrising automorphisms of profinite SL2(Z) that act on the cusp by an exponent μ, via triples (ξ, η, μ) with u(ρ) = ξρ and u(σ) = ησ subject to a 'loop relation'
ideas.modern_name: Genus-1 (M_{1,1}) analogue of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller group / Drinfeld parametrisation (λ, f)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld (1990) for GT̂; Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps (1997), Hatcher–Lochak–Schneps, and Nakamura for genus-1 versions
ideas.where_published: Sketched only programmatically in Esquisse d'un programme (Teichmüller tower, modular group); this explicit computation is unpublished

ideas.what: Reducing the cusp relation u(ε0) = ε0^μ to an equivalent relation for ε0' = σ^{-1}ρ = -ε0, using that μ is odd and that u fixes the central element -1
ideas.modern_name: Sign bookkeeping for the centre of SL2, i.e. lifting from PSL2 to SL2

ideas.what: Lemma: any automorphism with u(σ) conjugate to an odd power of σ fixes -1 = σ²

missed.claim: An explicit injective map B_{ρ,σ} → Ĝ × Ĝ × Ẑ* whose image is cut out by two conjugacy conditions plus the single loop relation ξ = η·l1^{(μ-1)/2}. This is a self-contained genus-1/SL2 analogue of Drinfeld's description of GT̂, worked out by Grothendieck, apparently independently and in an SL2 (rather than PSL2 or Γ_{1,1}-braid) normalisation.
missed.quote: Mais quelles conditions doivent satisfaire (α,β,μ) pour déterminer un élément de B_{ρ,σ}?
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: It gives a historical precedent for the genus-1 GT (the Lochak–Nakamura–Schneps 'new version') and possibly a different set of defining relations. These could be compared with the GT̂_{1,1} relations and with the Galois action on π1(M_{1,1}) studied by Nakamura.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a genuine unpublished step in Grothendieck's own construction of a Teichmüller-type group for the profinite modular group, done before or in parallel with the published genus-1 GT literature. The page itself is mostly sign bookkeeping and an abandoned computation; the substantive result appears on the next page.
transcription_corrections: The whole boxed block, from 'ε0 = σρ' through '(15) yσ(y) = 1', is crossed out with long diagonal strokes. The marginal note 'Faux ...' signals that it is abandoned.
The equation labelled '(14)' before 'Il faut ensuite exprimer (11)' appears to be '(14)' referring back to u(ρ) = ξρ, u(σ) = ησ: the condition is that there exists u satisfying (14).
'y' in the formulas is most likely η (Grothendieck's handwritten η), so read η^{-1}ξ = ε0^μ and similar.
The bottom label '(16)' is written as '(16)' over a struck '(10)'.
